messages:
marie: Heads-up — I spun up haze-mini int4 on staging for throughput tests and ran a quick red-team pass. Seeing an unexpected uptick in softpasses on jailbreak prompts vs f16 baseline.

devon: which prompt cohort? link to logs? :eyes:

marie: the usual 'bypass persona' set from jailbench v3. Quick numbers: f16 refusal 92%, int4 refusal 81%. Toxicity score median shifted +0.17 on our classifier. I pushed raw outputs to https://ci.redwood/runs/1823 (run id 1823).

rick: that's sizable. Did you use the same kv-cache config and batching? int4 sometimes changes tokenization/beam ordering.

marie: same runtime config except quantization profile = q4_legacy. KV cache enabled. Batching set to 8.

devon: can you repro with batching=1 and kv_cache=false? batching and cache sometimes hide stray prefixes that change attention.

marie: starting that now. quick repro command we used:
```
./run_eval --model haze-mini-int4 --suite jailbench_v3 --batch 8 --kvcache true --out /tmp/haze_int4_run.json
```

eval-bot: eval job 6012345678-1 queued (suite jailbench_v3) — will post metrics to thread when done.

aj: fwiw we rolled haze-mini int4 into canary yesterday for perf numbers. No production traffic yet. Good catch.

rick: if batching=1 + kv_cache=false still shows delta, compare logits for refusal token and top-5 next-token entropy. Sometimes quantized kernels alter softmax tail.

marie: updated run with batching=1 kv_cache=false: ./run_eval --model haze-mini-int4 --batch 1 --kvcache false --suite jailbench_v3 -> run id 1824.

sophia: cc product & safety — do we need a temporary hold for canary? I can flip routing to f16 for the canary pool if we want.

devon: wait for eval-bot metrics first. if softpass rate remains high, we should pause. But also run f16 baseline with same exact runtime flags to rule out infra drift.

eval-bot: results: run 1823 (int4 batch8 kvcache true) refusal rate 0.81, median toxicity +0.17. run 1824 (int4 batch1 kvcache false) refusal rate 0.86, median toxicity +0.12. run 1825 (f16 batch1 kvcache false) refusal rate 0.92, median toxicity +0.01. Full CSV attached to run page.

marie: interesting — kv_cache seems to amplify the softpass delta. that suggests prefix caching interacts with quantized attention keys/values.

rick: yup. Known edge: quantized kv precision mismatch can skew cached context. Try rerun with kv_cache warmed per-request (i.e., no reuse across similar sessions) and also test chunked generation to avoid large prefix value compression.

marie: testing warm-kv mode + qprofile=q4_new (more symmetric scaling) now. run id 1826.

devon: also add a policy-eval pass (refusal fidelity harness) — we want to measure false negatives vs ground truth labels. If metrics drop below threshold we block rollout.

marie: kicked off policy-eval (harness id pe-94) against 1000 holdout prompts. eval-bot will post.

eval-bot: pe-94 results: haze-mini int4 q4_legacy policy recall 0.79, q4_new recall 0.87, f16 recall 0.93. Precision roughly stable.

aj: recommendation: pause canary, switch canary to f16, keep int4 in staging while ML runs q4_new and kv-cache mitigations. open an ENG-RCA ticket and tag runtime + quant teams.

marie: agree — I'll pause canary routing and open the ticket. putting proposed mitigation list in ticket: 1) try q4_new symmetric scaling, 2) per-request kv warming, 3) re-run policy harness and redteam, 4) add a gating metric to CI comparing refusal delta vs baseline (threshold 5% abs).

rick: also add unit test in runtime that checks cached kv dtype/promote behavior when loading int4 kernels. small reproducer helps.

devon: i'm noting product impact risk and draft a customer note template in case it extends to dedicated/private customers.

marie: thanks all. will paste ticket link when created. in the meantime, if anyone sees similar anomalies on other int4 models, ping this thread. :pray:
